12	/-!
13	# The (C2) effectivity theorem and the surjectivity close
14	
15	**The campaign close.**  The fppf-effectivity theorem of the (C2) campaign (Kleiman,
16	*The Picard Scheme*, `th:cmp` Part 2 recast on the cocycle model) and the resulting
17	bijectivity of the unit of the étale plus construction over section-admitting field
18	tests:
19	
20	* `Over.exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq_of_pieces` — effectivity for an arbitrary
21	  faithfully flat `A → B`, given a covering family of trivialized pieces: a rigidified
22	  class on the cover curve whose two coprojection pullbacks agree on the nose descends
23	  along the cover inclusion `cg`.  The σ-normalized comparison exists unconditionally
24	  (E1); flat trivializations come from the trivialized pieces by localize-and-flatten;
25	  the refinement splice assembles the descent.
26	* `Over.exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq` — **the (C2) effectivity theorem** for a
27	  module-finite faithfully flat cover: the covering family of trivialized pieces is
28	  produced *unconditionally* by the moving lemma
29	  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.EffectivityMoving`).  Module-finiteness is honest: for a
30	  merely quasi-finite étale cover the bare restricted class need not trivialize on any
31	  saturated piece (see the moving lemma's docstring); the close below reaches arbitrary
32	  étale covers of a field test through the field cofinality of étale covers.
33	* `PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section` — **the headline**: over a field test `K`
34	  admitting a curve point `σ : Spec K ⟶ C`, the unit of the étale plus construction is
35	  surjective.  A plus class is represented on a finite separable field-extension cover
36	  (`Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`); the rigidification layer
37	  (G1 + the rigidified transport keystone) puts the representative in the effectivity
38	  theorem's hypotheses; the descended class maps to the original by `mk`-calculus.
39	* `PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section` — with the (C1) injectivity (étale separatedness),
40	  the unit is a group isomorphism `relPic C (Spec K) ≃* PicEtAff C K`.
41	-/

43	set_option autoImplicit false
44	
45	universe u
46	
47	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
48	  TopologicalSpace CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups
49

51	
52	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
53	
54	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
55	variable (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
56	variable [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]

67	set_option quotPrecheck false in
68	local notation "u₁" => (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap (tensorInl (A := A) (B := B))).left
69	set_option quotPrecheck false in
70	local notation "u₂" => (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap (tensorInr (A := A) (B := B))).left
71	set_option quotPrecheck false in
72	local notation "cg" => (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId A B).restrictScalars k)).left

74	namespace Over
75	
76	variable [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B] (σ : overSpec k A ⟶ C)
77	
78	/-- **(C2) effectivity from a covering family of trivialized pieces** (arbitrary
79	faithfully flat cover): a class on the cover curve represented by `γ`, rigidified along
80	the base-changed section and with equal coprojection pullbacks on the nose, descends
81	along `cg` — provided every point of the base curve lies in an affine piece on which
82	the representing cocycle trivializes. -/
83	theorem exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq_of_pieces
84	    (𝒩 : (XB).PointedCover) (γ : (XB).unitsCocycle 𝒩)
85	    (hrig : Over.IsRigidified
86	      (Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId A B).restrictScalars k) ≫ σ)
87	      (Scheme.CechPic.mk 𝒩 γ.class))
88	    (hdesc : Scheme.CechPic.map (u₁) (Scheme.CechPic.mk 𝒩 γ.class)
89	        = Scheme.CechPic.map (u₂) (Scheme.CechPic.mk 𝒩 γ.class))
90	    (hpieces : ∀ x : XA, ∃ (V : (XA).Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen V), x ∈ V ∧
91	      Nonempty (PieceTrivialization C 𝒩 γ V)) :
92	    ∃ M : (XA).CechPic,
93	      Scheme.CechPic.map (cg) M = Scheme.CechPic.mk 𝒩 γ.class := by
94	  obtain ⟨W⟩ := exists_normalizedCechComparison C σ 𝒩 γ hrig hdesc
95	  refine exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq_of_flat C σ W fun x => ?_
96	  obtain ⟨V₁, hV₁, hxV₁, ⟨T₁⟩⟩ := hpieces x
97	  obtain ⟨V, hV, hxV, T, hT⟩ :=
98	    exists_flat_pieceTrivialization_of_le C σ W hV₁ T₁ hxV₁
99	  exact ⟨V, hV, hxV, T, hT⟩
100	
101	/-- **The (C2) effectivity theorem** (recon §0.3; Kleiman `th:cmp` Part 2, the descent
102	of the rigidified pair): for a module-finite faithfully flat cover `A → B` of the test
103	algebra of a curve point `σ`, every Čech Picard class on the cover curve `X_B` that is
104	rigidified along the base-changed section (`hrig`) and has equal coprojection pullbacks
105	on the curve over `B ⊗[A] B` (`hdesc`) descends along the cover inclusion:
106	`∃ M, cg^* M = L`. -/
107	theorem exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq [Module.Finite A B]
108	    (L : (XB).CechPic)
109	    (hrig : Over.IsRigidified
110	      (Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId A B).restrictScalars k) ≫ σ) L)
111	    (hdesc : Scheme.CechPic.map (u₁) L = Scheme.CechPic.map (u₂) L) :
112	    ∃ M : (XA).CechPic, Scheme.CechPic.map (cg) M = L := by
113	  induction L using Scheme.CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒩 a
114	  induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ
115	  rw [show (Quot.mk _ γ : (XB).unitsH1 𝒩)
116	    = CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle.class γ from rfl] at hrig hdesc ⊢
117	  refine exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq_of_pieces C σ 𝒩 γ hrig hdesc fun x => ?_
118	  obtain ⟨V, hV, hxV, h1⟩ := Over.exists_isAffineOpen_cechPicMap_preimage_eq_one
119	    (B := B) C (Scheme.CechPic.mk 𝒩 γ.class) x
120	  exact ⟨V, hV, hxV, Over.pieceTrivialization_of_cechPicMap_eq_one C V h1⟩
121	
122	end Over
123	
124	end effectivity

126	/-! ## The surjectivity close (recon §0.2) -/
127	
128	section close
129	
130	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
131	
132	/-- **Surjectivity of the unit of the étale plus construction over a section-admitting
133	field test** (Kleiman 2.5(2), axiom (C2) — the campaign headline): if the curve admits
134	a `K`-point `σ`, every class of `PicEtAff C K` comes from a relative Picard class.
135	
136	A representative on an étale cover of `Spec K` is refined to a finite separable field
137	extension (field cofinality); the rigidification layer produces a rigidified Čech
138	representative whose descent equation holds on the nose; the (C2) effectivity theorem
139	descends it along the cover inclusion; and the `relPicMk`/`mk`-calculus identifies the
140	descended class's unit with the original plus class. -/
141	theorem PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section (σ : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
142	    Function.Surjective (PicEtAff.unit C K) := by
143	  intro q
144	  induction q using PicEtAff.ind with | _ E x
145	  classical
146	  -- ### refine the representing cover to a finite separable field extension
147	  obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hLalg, hLfin, hLsep, ⟨f⟩⟩ :=
148	    E.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
149	  set F : Algebra.EtaleCover K := Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L with hF
150	  set g : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] F.Carrier :=
151	    ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom).comp f with hg
152	  set y : descentClasses C F := descentMap C g x with hy
153	  have hq : PicEtAff.mk C E x = PicEtAff.mk C F y :=
154	    (PicEtAff.mk_descentMap C g x).symm
155	  haveI : Module.Finite K F.Carrier :=
156	    Module.Finite.equiv (R := K) (M := L)
157	      (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toLinearEquiv
158	  -- ### a rigidified representative of the descent class (G1)
159	  obtain ⟨Lc, hrig, hLcrep⟩ := relPic.exists_isRigidified_rep
160	    (Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId K F.Carrier).restrictScalars k) ≫ σ)
161	    (y : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier))
162	  have hmem : relPicMk C (overSpec k F.Carrier) Lc ∈ descentClasses C F := by
163	    rw [hLcrep]
164	    exact y.2
165	  -- ### the on-the-nose descent equation (the rigidified transport keystone)
166	  have hdesc0 := Over.IsRigidified.cechPicMap_doubleInl_eq_doubleInr σ hmem hrig
167	  have hinl : doubleInl (k := k) F = tensorInl (k := k) (A := K) (B := F.Carrier) :=
168	    AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl
169	  have hinr : doubleInr (k := k) F = tensorInr (k := k) (A := K) (B := F.Carrier) :=
170	    AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl
171	  rw [hinl, hinr] at hdesc0
172	  -- ### the effectivity theorem
173	  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := Over.exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq C σ Lc hrig hdesc0
174	  refine ⟨relPicMk C (overSpec k K) M, ?_⟩
175	  -- ### the `mk`-calculus close
176	  rw [PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk C F (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) M)]
177	  rw [hq]
178	  refine congrArg (PicEtAff.mk C F) (Subtype.ext ?_)
179	  change relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.ofId K F.Carrier).restrictScalars k)
180	      (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) M) = (y : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier))
181	  rw [relPicAlgMap, relPicMap_mk, hM, hLcrep]
182	
183	/-- **The unit of the étale plus construction is an isomorphism over a
184	section-admitting field test** — étale separatedness (C1) plus effectivity (C2):
185	`relPic C (Spec K) ≃* PicEtAff C K`. -/
186	noncomputable def PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section (σ : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
187	    relPic C (overSpec k K) ≃* PicEtAff C K :=
188	  MulEquiv.ofBijective (PicEtAff.unit C K)
189	    ⟨PicEtAff.unit_injective C K, PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section C K σ⟩
190	
191	end close

9	/-!
10	# (C1) étale separatedness of the relative Picard functor — assembly file
11	
12	This file is the future home of the **(C1) étale-separatedness** theorem — injectivity of
13	the unit of the étale plus construction,
14	
15	```
16	theorem PicEtAff.unit_injective : Function.Injective (PicEtAff.unit C A)
17	```
18	
19	for a curve `C` (proper, geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced) over a field
20	`k` — which is the separatedness half of Kleiman, *The Picard Scheme*, Theorem 2.5(1): the
21	relative Picard presheaf is a separated presheaf for the étale topology, so its
22	sheafification (the one-step plus `PicEtAff`) has an injective unit. The assembly follows
23	the "Refined design" of `informal/c1-etale-separatedness-assembly.md` (the ζ-decomposition
24	of the scheme-side step ε3/ζ), consuming brick 3 (`Over.prPullback_injective`), the
25	projection-descent equivalence (ε1, `Picard/ProjectionUnits.lean`), the composite unit
26	descent (ε2, `Descent/UnitDescentComposite.lean`) and the dictionary naturality (γ,
27	`Picard/CechPicToPicNaturality.lean`).
28	
29	## What is landed here (ζ1)
30	
31	`AlgebraicGeometry.Over.cechPicMap_tensorInl_eq_tensorInr`, the **class-level coherence
32	seed**: if a Čech Picard class `L` on the curve-product `C ⊗ Spec A` restricts, over a test
33	algebra `A → B`, to something pulled back from the base — i.e. `p_B^* N = (C ◁ Spec f)^* L`
34	for `N : CechPic (Spec B)` and `f = ofId A B` — then the two base changes of `N` to
35	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B)` agree along the two coprojections `tensorInl, tensorInr : B →ₐ[k] B ⊗[A] B`.
36	Both sides pull back along `p_{B ⊗[A] B}` to the same restriction of `L`
37	(`Scheme.CechPic.map_comp` + `Over.snd_left_naturality` + `Over.overSpecMap_comp`), and
38	pullback along the curve projection is injective (brick 3), so they are equal. This is the
39	"one genuinely delicate step" reduced to its cocycle-free seed — the honest descent datum is
40	built downstream (ζ2).
41	
42	## Remaining steps of the assembly (per the worksheet)
43	
44	* **ζ2 (construct the composite descent unit)**: choose a basic (Zariski) cover `f : ι → B`
45	  trivializing `toPic N`, build `v ∈ ((∏ Sᵢ) ⊗[A] (∏ Sᵢ))ˣ` whose collapse is the cover
46	  cocycle of `N` and whose cross terms are ζ1's comparison descended through ε1, and prove
47	  `Module.IsDescentCocycle v` by checking the two conditions after `p`-pullback (ε1
48	  injectivity), where they are coboundary computations for one cocycle representative of `L`.
49	* **ζ3 (close)**: `M := cechPicEquivPic.symm (picClass v)` over `A`; establish `p_A^* M = L`
50	  by the `unitsRes`/`mk_eq_one_iff` calculus (the fppf `descend_coboundary` analogue), then
51	  unfold to `PicEtAff.unit_injective` through `injective_iff_map_eq_one` + `mk_eq_mk_iff` +
52	  `relPicMk` calculus.
53	
54	## Main declarations (this file)
55	
56	* `AlgebraicGeometry.tensorInl`, `AlgebraicGeometry.tensorInr` — the two `k`-algebra
57	  coprojections `B →ₐ[k] B ⊗[A] B` (mirroring `doubleInl`/`doubleInr` of
58	  `Picard/PicEtAff.lean` for a general test algebra `B`), with the diagonal-coherence lemma
59	  `AlgebraicGeometry.tensorInl_comp_ofId`.
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.cechPicMap_tensorInl_eq_tensorInr` — sub-brick ζ1.
61	-/

78	`k → A → B`), the `A`- and `k`-scalar actions commute. Needed so that
79	`Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft` elaborates as a `k`-algebra map into `B ⊗[A] B` and so

/-!
# Zariski separation of the étale plus construction

The affine étale Picard functor `PicEtAff C ·` is a separated presheaf for the Zariski
topology of affine tests: two plus classes over `A` agreeing on every member of a finite
basic-open cover of `Spec A` agree (`AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.eq_of_away_eq`).

Route: the plus construction of *any* presheaf is separated — representatives agreeing
on each localization agree on an étale cover assembled from the local witnessing covers,
and the finite product of the witnessing carriers is again an étale cover of the base.
The gluing across the factors of the product is the relative Picard decomposition of a
finite product of test algebras (`AlgebraicGeometry.relPic.eq_of_pi_proj_eq`,
`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicPi`).

The file also provides `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.exists_relPicAlgMap_eq_of_mapAlg_eq`,
the representative-level unfolding of an equality of restricted plus classes, consumed
by the gluing half (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtAffZariskiGlue`).
-/
/-! ## Unfolding an equality of restricted plus classes -/


########## PicEtAffZariskiGlue.lean ##########
/-!
# Zariski gluing of the étale plus construction

The gluing half of the Zariski sheaf property of the affine étale Picard functor: a
family of plus classes on a finite basic-open cover of `Spec A`, compatible on the
pairwise overlaps, glues to a plus class on `A`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.exists_mapAlg_eq_of_compat`).

The engine is the **pair condition** (`PicEtAff.relPicAlgMap_tensor_eq_of_compat`): for
descent-class representatives `ξ₁, ξ₂` of two compatible classes over localizations
`S₁, S₂` of `A`, the two pullbacks to the `A`-tensor product of the covering carriers
agree.  The overlap compatibility supplies a common refinement over the overlap
localization; base-changing it to the tensor product and transporting through
`AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap_congr` (the two routes into the base change are
semilinear over the *same* localization, and `A`-algebra maps out of a localization are
unique) reduces the claim to injectivity of relative Picard restriction along an étale
cover — the (C1) corollary
(`AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap_injective_of_etaleCover`).  This is the single point
where the Layer-2 functoriality consumes étale separatedness.

**The kernel lemma** (`AlgebraicGeometry.Over.exists_cechPic_map_snd_of_ker_whiskerLeft`):
for a proper, geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced curve `C` over `k` and
a faithfully flat tower `A → B` of `k`-algebras, every Čech Picard class on
`X_A = (C ⊗ Spec A).left` killed by the base-change pullback `cg^*` is pulled back from
`Spec A`.  Route: extract a trivializing `0`-cochain `β` from the kernel hypothesis;
produce the descent unit `w` (ζ3 brick W, `exists_kernelDescentUnit`); represent its
descended class by a cover/cocycle/`μ` triple (ζ3 brick M, `descentClassRep`); glue and
descend the cobounding units on an affine refinement (ζ3 brick G,
`exists_kernelCobounding`); verify the coboundary relation by injectivity of `cg`-pullback
and the `transition` field (`kernelCobounding_rel`); conclude by `mk_eq_mk_iff`.

**The close** (`AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.unit_injective`, Kleiman 2.5(1), axiom (C1)):
the unit of the étale plus construction of the relative Picard functor is injective on
every affine test algebra — the étale separatedness of `PicEtAff`.
-/

########## CechKernelGlue.lean ##########
/-!
# The glued cobounding units of the Čech kernel lemma (ζ3 brick G)

Let `E = [lam]` be a Čech class on `X_A = (C ⊗ Spec A).left` killed by the base-change
pullback `cg^*`, trivialized by a `0`-cochain `β` on the pulled-back cover, with descent
unit `w` (ζ3 brick W) and Čech representative `(𝒞, d, μ)` of its descended class (ζ3
brick M).  For every point `s` and affine open `U ≤ ℰ_s ⊓ p_A⁻¹𝒞_{p_A s}`, this file
glues the local units

`gluePiece = β_x⁻¹ ⋅ (cg^♯ lam_{cg x, s})⁻¹ ⋅ (p_B^♯ μ_{p_A s})⁻¹`

over the cover `{𝒜_x ⊓ cg⁻¹U}` of `cg⁻¹U` (they agree on overlaps by the coboundary
relation of `β` and the cocycle identity of `lam`), shows the glued unit has equal
coprojection pullbacks (by the local ratio form of `w` and the `ratio` field of the
representative), and descends it through `cg` to a unit `c` on `U`
(`Over.exists_kernelCobounding`) — the cobounding `0`-cochain of the kernel lemma.

All data is carried in declaration signatures (never in `variable` commands with
local-notation types).
-/

########## KernelDescentUnit.lean ##########
/-!
# The descent unit of a Čech class killed by the base change (ζ3 brick W)

Let `C` be proper, geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced over a field `k`,
and `A → B` a tower of `k`-algebras.  A Čech Picard class on `X_A = (C ⊗ Spec A).left`
killed by the base-change pullback `cg^*` is trivialized by a unit `0`-cochain `β` on
the pulled-back cover.  The ratio of the two coprojection pullbacks of `β` to
`X_{B ⊗[A] B}` is compatible on overlaps, so it glues to a global unit and descends
through the projection (ε1 at `⊤`, ζ2·P) to a global unit `w` on `Spec (B ⊗[A] B)`; `w`
satisfies the Amitsur cocycle identity — checked after pullback to the triple-tensor
curve product, where the telescope of `β`-ratios cancels along the simplicial
coincidences — and restricts to `1` along the diagonal, so through `ΓSpecIso` its
avatar is a descent `1`-cocycle (`Module.IsDescentCocycle`).

Main declaration: `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.exists_kernelDescentUnit`.  The kernel-lemma
assembly (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.CechKernelLemma`) consumes `w` twice: its Picard
class over `A` is the descended class, and the recorded local form of `p₂^♯ w` makes
the `μ`-corrected trivialization of the ratio class descend through
`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SectionsDescent`.
-/

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DegreeZero
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap
8	
9	/-!
10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
11	
12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
33	-/

42	
43	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
44	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
45

48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
49	
50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
57	
58	section DegAt
59	
60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
61	
62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
63	@[simp]
64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
67	
68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))

8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-5: the coverage obligation is Zariski-local in the test, so AFFINE tests suffice
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` reduced `ChartsCoverLocally` — and with it
12	antecedent 2 of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` — to pointwise data at **every test scheme
13	`T`**.  That is where the reduction chain stops, and the quantifier it stops at is the
14	problem this file addresses.
15	
16	**Every divisor-side producer in this project is indexed by a RING, not by a scheme.**
17	`DivFamZar C S π n` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyZar.lean:235`) is a quotient of local-equation
18	systems over an algebra `S`; `divFamZar C π n T` at a general test
19	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyZarVehicle.lean:187`) is the affine-opens *limit* of those, and the
20	comparison `divFamZarAffineEquiv` (:300) collapses it to `DivFamZar` only on an affine
21	test.  Likewise every producer of a certified family, of an effective witness
22	(`DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:147`), and every classifier
23	(`effectiveDivisorClassifyZar`, :217) is stated over a ring or a field.  So a coverage
24	lane facing "for every scheme `T`" has to cross the affine-to-general gap **before** it can
25	use any of that machinery, and nothing said it was allowed to skip it.
26	
27	It is allowed to skip it, and that is this file's content.
28	
29	## Why locality in the test is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
30	
31	The naive argument — "sieves are local, so restrict to an affine cover" — is not available
32	as stated, because `ChartsCoverLocally` is a statement about the sieve on `T` itself, and
33	the pointwise hypothesis quantifies over points of `T`.  Three things have to be checked,
34	and each is where the argument could fail:
35	
36	* **the class must restrict.**  The datum at a point `t` of an affine piece `Y` is about a
37	  section over an open of `Y`, while the obligation at `t : ↥T` is about an open of `T`.
38	  Composing `W.ι ≫ 𝒰.f j` gives a map into `T` but not an *open of* `T`, so the transport
39	  cannot be done at the level of `T.Opens` — it has to be done at the level of the sieve,
40	  where an arbitrary morphism is allowed;
41	* **the sieve must be transitive.**  Membership of `⨆ i, imageSieve (f i) s` in the
42	  topology on `T` is deduced from membership of its *pullbacks* along the cover maps, which
43	  is `GrothendieckTopology.transitive` plus `Presheaf.pullback_imageSieve` — the latter is
44	  what says the pullback of an image sieve is the image sieve of the restricted section,
45	  i.e. that the obligation at `Y` is about `s|_Y` and nothing else;
46	* **the pullback must commute with the supremum.**  `Sieve.pullback` is a left adjoint on
47	  sieves, so it preserves `iSup`; without that the per-piece obligations would be about a
48	  different sieve than the one the pullback of the target names.
49	
50	None of the three mentions `pic⁰`, a chart, or a divisor.  That is the point: the
51	affine-to-general passage for antecedent 2 is a fact about the site, and mixing it with the
52	geometry is what made it look like part of the geometry's price.
53	
54	## What this does and does not buy
55	
56	It buys the quantifier, and only the quantifier.  `chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` below
57	asks for the pointwise datum **only over affine schemes**, and produces
58	`ChartsCoverLocally` at every test; `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_affine` composes that
59	with B-6.  So a producer may now assume its test is `Spec S` and reach for
60	`divFamZarAffineEquiv`, `DivisorFamilyFieldSurj`, `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar` and the rest
61	of the ring-indexed machinery directly.
62	
63	It does **not** produce the datum at an affine test.  That is B-5's geometry and it remains
64	open; per `Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` and the `dat-b` row the residue there is
65	the class-side question, and per `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean` the range containment `hV` is
66	a further separate obligation.  What changes is that the residue is now stated where the
67	tree's producers live.
68	
69	**On the converse, corrected.**  An earlier version of this paragraph said
70	`affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally` makes the affine and general forms "equivalent", and cited
71	that as discharging the `reduction-needs-its-converse` safeguard.  It does not: that
72	declaration is `rfl`-equal to `pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally`, its `[IsAffine Y]` binder is
73	never used, and the direction it certifies is the *free* one — general pointwise data gives the
74	affine data by `fun Y _ s y => h Y s y`.  So the affine form is a genuine **weakening** of the
75	general one, which is exactly why `chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` is worth having; the
76	honest certificate is that theorem, not a no-op converse (audit `I-1023`).  The converse is
77	kept only as the affine-test instance of the pointwise extraction, which is what it is.
78	
79	**On the atlas, and this is the sharper limit.**  Nothing here pins `V`.  The statements below
80	take an arbitrary family `f`, which is what makes the site content reusable — but a consumer
81	must supply coverage at the *same* `V` at which antecedent 1 was certified, and `ajcr-p1`
82	measured both ends of that range to be bad: `hf` is free at `V = ⊥` (`isChartUniv_bot`, with a
83	construction that never mentions the Abel chart), while `V = ⊤` returns the unrestricted
84	certificate that three headers call false.  So any workable `V` is a proper intermediate open,
85	CHART-U(b)'s openness is load-bearing, and the pair `(huniv V, hcov V)` has **no measured
86	inhabitant at any `V`** (`I-1012`).  Two bad endpoints are two refutations, not a non-vacuity
87	check.

92	  presheaf and no chart: a sieve on `T` is covering as soon as its pullback along every map
93	  from an affine scheme in a cover of `T` is covering.
94	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` — **the reduction**: pointwise
95	  coverage over affine tests only gives `ChartsCoverLocally` at every test.
96	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_affine` — the composite with B-6, i.e.

99	  is not a strengthening.

152	    (h : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (y : ↥Y),
153	      ∃ (W : Y.Opens) (_ : y ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
154	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
155	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
156	  intro T s
157	  refine mem_zariskiTopology_of_pullback_affine _ fun j => ?_
158	  -- the pullback of the supremum is the supremum of the pullbacks, and each is the image
159	  -- sieve of the RESTRICTED section — so the obligation at the affine piece is exactly the
160	  -- affine instance of the hypothesis
161	  have hpb : (⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i) s).pullback (T.affineCover.f j)
162	      = ⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i)

structure ChartFibrePresented {X T : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    where
  /-- The locus of the test where the class named by `g` is a chart value. -/
  W : T.Opens
  /-- The chart point over that locus. -/
  r : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X
  /-- The square commutes: `r` names the class `g` restricted to `W`. -/
  sq : yoneda.map r ≫ f = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
  /-- **Coverage on the locus**: an `S`-point of `X` and an `S`-point of `T` carrying the
  same class factor through `W`, compatibly with both projections. -/
  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : S ⟶ X) (w : S ⟶ T),
    f.app (op S) v = g.app (op S) w → ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}), u ≫ r = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w

namespace ChartFibrePresented

variable {X T : Scheme.{u}} {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
  {g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}

/-- **The datum presents the fibre product**: the square of `ChartFibrePresented` is a
pullback of presheaves.

Pullbacks in a presheaf category are computed pointwise
(`IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app`), and a pointwise pullback of types is exactly
"commutes + jointly injective + jointly surjective" (`Types.isPullback_iff`).  The first is
`sq`, the third is `exists_factor`, and the second is free from `W.ι` being a
monomorphism — which is where the openness of `W` does its work. -/
theorem isPullback (D : ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
    IsPullback (yoneda.map D.r) (yoneda.map D.W.ι) f g := by
  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 =>
      φ.app S) D.sq
  · -- joint injectivity: already forced by `W.ι` alone, being a monomorphism
    rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
    have : u₁ ≫ D.W.ι = u₂ ≫ D.W.ι := h₂
    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp this
  · -- joint surjectivity: `exists_factor` at the test `S.unop`
    intro v w hvw
    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩

end ChartFibrePresented

/-- **THE CRITERION** — `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` from elementwise data, discharging BOTH
clauses of `MorphismProperty.relative` at once.

Given, for every test point of the target sheaf, a `ChartFibrePresented` datum, the chart map
is an open immersion of presheaves.  Certificate-free, divRep-free, and with no reference to
divisors: the input is a family of opens of tests together with the coverage statement on
each.

This is the honest shape of `IsChartUniv`'s obligation.  Reading `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
as a single "relative GAP-2" statement conflates:

* **relative representability** — that the fibre product is a scheme at all.  Supplied here
  by `W`, an open subscheme of the test, and proved by `ChartFibrePresented.isPullback`;
* **the property clause** — that each represented pullback is an open immersion.  Supplied
  here by `W.ι` being an open immersion, which is free.

What is *not* free, and is the whole mathematical content, is `exists_factor`: a class that
agrees with a chart value must come from the locus.  For the Abel chart that is the relative
form of DAT-C GAP-2 (uniqueness of the normalized effective representative) fed through the
classifier — so the CERT-Σ gate is real, but it gates ONE field of ONE structure rather than
the whole certificate. -/
theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
      ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f := by
  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists fun T g => ?_
